propositions: The autouse repository-isolation guard's head() probe times out at the fixed five-second watchdog during full-suite concurrent execution despite passing in sequential runs.
Real probe latency under full-suite load (18 processes) reaches p99 2.08s and max 3.30s, with 16 probes exceeding 1 second, but none exceeding 5 seconds in instrumented observation.

Host scheduler and filesystem starvation under severe oversubscription (load p99 138.2 on 18 CPUs, process count max 771) correlates with slow probes and process-spawn failures (OSError: no resources to fork).
Sequential probe latency (p50 9.6ms, max 507ms) and controlled concurrency experiments reject PATH contamination, Git-environment corruption, and test-state inheritance as root causes.
The five-second watchdog contract from callous-amused-hart remains valid and evidence does not support raising the bound without explicit operator design decision and safe calibration proof.
